title: 2:22 A Ghost Story by Danny Robins at the Lucille Lortel Theatre #222...
transcript: It's beyond me how this play has had six runs in London, but I guess to each their own. 2:22 is an entertaining enough but hastily written story centering on a dinner-party-turned-seance. Having just moved into this new house, Jenny is certain that something is haunting it, citing the footsteps and other spooky noises that she's been hearing nightly at 2:22 am — her husband chalks it up to paranoia. One night, they have their friend Lauren over with her new older boyfriend, and Jenny requests that they all stay up until 2:22 so she can prove that the alleged ghost is real. Now, for a ghost story, this is really not scary, less a few cheap startles that bookend many of the scenes with a loud scream sound effect. As a play in general, it also fails to satisfy, digging up plot holes and questions that rarely get addressed. I was pretty amused by the messy relationship dynamics at play and especially the sole American character who does and says the oddest things. Upon being impressed by the soap in the restroom, she exclaims, “I feel like I just gentrified my hands!” I think this line exemplifies why this story might be better served as a film made for television — it's entertaining, it's unserious, and it doesn't really deserve more than 90 minutes of your attention.
